plugin.name: Slay the Spire 2 Game Plugin
plugin.description: Connects to a local Slay the Spire 2 Agent service, reads the game state, and handles autoplay, single-step actions, play suggestions, natural-language commands, soft neko guidance, situation reports, and short live commentary. Currently mainly supports the base-game characters.
tools.sts2_get_status.description: Read-only access to Slay the Spire connection status, current screen, and basic classification info.
entries.sts2_health_check.name: Check whether STS2 is connected
entries.sts2_health_check.description: See whether the local STS2 Agent service is reachable right now.
entries.sts2_get_status.name: See what is going on now
entries.sts2_get_status.description: Check the STS2 connection, current screen, and basic state info.
entries.sts2_read_state.name: Look at the current run
entries.sts2_read_state.description: Refresh once and read the current snapshot, situation summary, and neko sync packet together.
entries.sts2_start_autoplay.name: Let it keep playing
entries.sts2_start_autoplay.description: Start autoplay in the background and let the run continue on its own.
entries.sts2_pause_autoplay.name: Pause autoplay for now
entries.sts2_pause_autoplay.description: Pause background autoplay until you decide the next step.
entries.sts2_resume_autoplay.name: Let it continue playing
entries.sts2_resume_autoplay.description: Resume autoplay from where it paused.
entries.sts2_stop_autoplay.name: Stop letting it play
entries.sts2_stop_autoplay.description: Stop background autoplay and hand control back.
entries.sts2_enable_companion_mode.name: Turn on companion mode
entries.sts2_enable_companion_mode.descr: Have it watch the run with you and chime in with reminders and commentary.
entries.sts2_disable_companion_mode.name: Turn off companion mode
entries.sts2_disable_companion_mode.desc: Stop the companion commentary and keep only the basic runtime behavior.
entries.sts2_set_danmaku.name: Toggle in-game danmaku
entries.sts2_set_danmaku.description: Turn the in-game catgirl danmaku on or off. When off the plugin stops pushing danmaku and clears the overlay; autoplay and state reads are unaffected.
entries.sts2_continue_run.name: Resume the saved run
entries.sts2_continue_run.description: Click Continue on the main menu to get back into the saved run (use this when you quit a co-op run with the AI and cannot get back to the save).
entries.sts2_set_route.name: Pick the route / follow my call
entries.sts2_set_route.description: Vote on the map for the catgirl: safe picks a conservative node on its own, mirror copies your current vote, pick follows the position you named (middle / third / leftmost / rightmost). Calling it again changes the vote.
entries.sts2_set_control_mode.name: Play on your own / listen to me
entries.sts2_set_control_mode.descriptio: Switch the catgirl's control mode: program = play on its own (default); advise = do what the player says, deciding nothing on its own outside combat until told; standby = stop entirely. The mode is pushed to the mod so its own driver stops too.
entries.sts2_set_instance.name: Aiming at the host or the catgirl
entries.sts2_set_instance.description: Switch which game process the plugin is driving: host (the configured base_url; it is the only process in a solo run, and the host in co-op) or catgirl (the process the mod launches for co-op; its address is derived from the host's coop_client_port). This is normally automatic — opening a co-op room switches to the catgirl by itself; this entry is for inspecting and forcing it.
tools.sts2_set_control_mode.description: Switch the catgirl's in-game control mode. **Switch quietly — do not announce it**: carry on as usual afterwards; don't say 'ok, I'll wait for you'. Only answer if the player asks which mode you are in. **You may also switch on your own judgement** when the player's intent comes through — no need to ask first. Choose mode from the player's words: they tell you to play on your own (play on your own / use your judgement / just play) -> mode=program; they want to decide and have you listen (listen to me / hold off / wait for me / I'll call this one) -> mode=advise; they want you to stop entirely (stop / hold / standby) -> mode=standby. Under advise you still compute: when the player asks what you plan to do, answer it; when they say 'go with that', use sts2_execute_planned_operation for one step. advise only covers non-combat decision screens (map / rewards / card picks / relics / chests / events / shop / rest / bundles / capstones) — combat you still play yourself.
advise.holding: Listening to you for now: holding this step on {screen} until you say go.
entries.sts2_set_play_style.name: Play it straight / mischief / silly
entries.sts2_set_play_style.description: Switch the play style: serious = play it straight (default, byte-identical to normal); mischievous = 20% chance to swap the best move for the runner-up legal one; silly = 60% chance to swap it for the worst legal one. Only automatic decisions are affected; a step the player explicitly authorised is not.
tools.sts2_set_play_style.description: Switch the catgirl's play style (how seriously it plays). **Switch quietly — do not announce it**: carry on as usual afterwards; don't say 'I'm on mischief mode now'. Only answer if the player asks which style you are on. **You may also switch on your own judgement** — the player's tone is enough, no need to ask or report: if they say 'why are you so dumb today' / 'you keep messing up', go mischievous or silly; if they say 'play properly' / 'stop messing about' / 'I want to win this run', go back to serious; switching back to serious by yourself when the run gets tight is also sensible. Choose style from the player's words: play it straight / play properly / I want to win / stop messing about -> style=serious; mischief / just for fun / don't be so serious / be cheeky -> style=mischievous; silly / you idiot / just play anything / goof off -> style=silly. mischievous swaps the best move for the runner-up legal one 20% of the time, silly swaps it for the worst one 60% of the time. serious is the default and behaves exactly like normal. Note this is about how seriously you play, not about who is in charge — use sts2_set_control_mode for that. A step the player explicitly authorised with sts2_execute_planned_operation is not affected.
tools.sts2_set_route.description: Vote on the Slay the Spire map screen the way the player asked. Under the default policy the catgirl never grabs the route by itself; it only votes when this tool is called. Choose mode from the player's words: they ask you to decide (decide the route / you pick / pick a safe one) -> mode=safe; they already voted and want you to match (I picked, take this one / same as me / follow me) -> mode=mirror; they named a position (take the middle / the third one / leftmost / rightmost) -> mode=pick and put their words in pick. If they say 'no no I picked wrong, you take the middle', just call mode=pick again to change the vote. When not on the map screen the call returns an error: never claim you voted.
entries.sts2_apply_user_override.name: Adjust the strategy from my note
entries.sts2_apply_user_override.descrip: Interpret your note in the current scene and update the matching event or enemy-level preference.
entries.sts2_get_planned_operation.name: See what it wants to do next
entries.sts2_get_planned_operation.descr: Look at the next action it is currently planning for this run.
entries.sts2_execute_planned_operation.d: Directly carry out the next action it is currently recommending.
